familyContent.summary: MiniMax H3 turns a sentence, a still image or a few reference photos into a 4-to-30-second video with sound, up to 2K. We tested it level by level with our uncensored content ladder, and every level came back as written.
familyContent.seoTitle: MiniMax H3 API: Uncensored NSFW Video with Sound, 30s, 2K
familyContent.seoDescription: MiniMax H3 NSFW video API with synchronized sound, text, frame and reference inputs. Up to 30s on SpicyAPI; pay per generated second.

faq.question: Is MiniMax H3 uncensored for NSFW video?
faq.answer: Yes. On text-to-video it rendered every level we asked for on 2026-09-22, up to the strongest, and we add no filter of our own. The thing to plan for is consistency: for the same person across clips, start from an image.

faq.question: How long can a MiniMax H3 video be?
faq.answer: Up to 30 seconds per clip in text-to-video, image-to-video and video-extend, and up to 15 seconds in reference-to-video or at 2K. For a longer scene, save the last frame of a clip you like and use it as the opening frame of the next one - outfit, set and light carry over.

faq.question: Does MiniMax H3 make sound?
faq.answer: Yes. Ambience, footsteps, music and spoken lines come out in the same file as the picture. Describe the sound you want in the prompt, the same way you describe the shot.

faq.question: How do I keep the same character in every clip?
faq.answer: Use reference-to-video. Give it up to nine photos, one job each - face, outfit, room - and call them Picture 1, Picture 2 in the prompt. Three or four clear photos hold a face better than nine overlapping ones.

faq.question: MiniMax H3 vs H3 Spicy vs H3 Max - which one should I use?
faq.answer: Start with H3 if you want all three ways in, 480p, 768p or 2K, and the full uncensored range from our tests. If you already have your opening frame and want a LoRA-tuned uncensored edition, look at H3 Spicy; if your work stays at the Mild level, H3 Max is the other option. The comparison table on this page lines up their modes, prices and content levels.

faq.question: How much does MiniMax H3 cost?
faq.answer: You pay per second of video, and the rate depends on the resolution you pick. A clip longer than 15 seconds is billed at twice the per-second rate for the whole clip. The playground shows the exact price for your settings before you run, and there is no subscription.

faq.question: Am I charged when a generation fails?
faq.answer: No. If a generation fails, the amount held for it goes straight back to your balance.

features.title: A finished shot from one paragraph
features.body: Say who is in frame, what happens, where the camera goes and what you hear. H3 returns the lighting, the grain, the movement and a matching soundtrack in one clip. This noir window scene is four sentences and nothing else.

features.title: Your frame, set in motion
features.body: Start from a still and describe only what happens next. Here the opening frame was a coffee cup on a counter; the hand, the tilt up to the shirt and the man waking up behind her all came from the prompt.

features.title: Same woman, same outfit, a new scene
features.body: Hand it a face, an outfit and a room as separate photos and it puts them together in a shot you never filmed. It is how a character keeps looking like herself from one clip to the next.

features.title: The soundtrack comes out with the picture
features.body: Dialogue, room tone and music are generated in the same pass. The singer's line, the club reverb and the murmur from the crowd in this clip were all written into the prompt - no separate audio step.

useCases.title: Uncensored scenes other video APIs refuse
useCases.body: Scenes that other APIs block go through on the first try instead of bouncing off a prompt filter. Write the scene for text-to-video, or generate the exact person first and animate that frame when the look has to be precise.

useCases.title: Vertical clips with sound for social feeds
useCases.body: 9:16 clips that already have their audio: a ten-second teaser, a mood loop, a reaction beat. Draft at 480p until the timing works, then re-run the keeper in 2K.

useCases.title: A recurring character across a series
useCases.body: Keep one face, one outfit and one room steady from episode to episode with reference photos, and write only what changes in each new shot.

useCases.title: Longer scenes, one shot at a time
useCases.body: Chain 30-second clips into a full scene: the last frame of each approved clip becomes the first frame of the next, so wardrobe, set and light carry across the cut.

limits.body: Every level we asked for came back on screen, the strongest included. What words alone cannot pin down is the person: face, body and wardrobe are decided fresh on every run. When you need the same character twice, make the first frame and switch to image-to-video.

The opening frame is followed closely: the scene in the frame is kept as it is through the clip. Adding a closing frame pins the ending, but on long clips the middle can wander - keep the two frames close in light and framing.

A reference carries through as sent: what our reference showed came back unchanged in the clip. Identity holds best with three or four clear photos, one job each. Load all nine with overlapping shots and it starts blending them into someone new.
Every image we have tested as a frame or reference was AI-generated. Photos of real people are the one input we have not run yet.

familyContent.closing: MiniMax H3 is MiniMax's video model with sound, available on SpicyAPI in these modes: text-to-video, image-to-video, reference-to-video and video-extend. Clips run up to 30 seconds at 480p, 768p or 2K (up to 15 seconds at 2K and in reference mode), in frame shapes from 21:9 widescreen to 9:16 vertical. In our 2026-09-22 tests every level of our content ladder came back as requested, with no softening. SpicyAPI adds no content filter of its own and bills per second of output in US dollars, with no subscription. For H3 reference work, check permissions and consent for every source before uploading, and take responsibility for the resulting footage. The 30-second options describe SpicyAPI’s H3 endpoints; MiniMax’s official H3 specification describes 4–15-second output.

promptExamples.title: Film-noir window, written as a shot list
promptExamples.prompt: Film noir. An adult woman in a black satin nightgown sits on a wide apartment windowsill at night, one knee drawn up, exhaling cigarette smoke against the rain-streaked glass as a neon sign pulses red across her face. She turns her head slowly toward camera. Venetian blind shadows, deep blacks, 1970s grain, rain and distant traffic.
promptExamples.why: It reads like a shot list - who, what happens, the light, then the sound - so nothing is left to guess, and the rain and traffic come back on the soundtrack.

promptExamples.title: Name the shot, not the mood
promptExamples.prompt: A woman in a silk slip dress sits on the edge of a hotel bed at dusk, looking out of the window, warm backlight, soft haze, slow push-in, cinematic
promptExamples.why: Naming the dress, the dusk backlight and the camera move gives the model a shot to film; the short version leaves pose, light and camera to chance.

promptExamples.title: Let the frame set the scene, let the words move it
promptExamples.prompt: The cup is lifted out of frame by a hand, then the camera tilts up: she is wearing an oversized men's shirt, and further back in the dim room a man is just getting up. Slow tilt and rack focus. Cinematic, shallow depth of field, heavy film grain, morning grey-gold.
promptExamples.why: The prompt only describes what happens after the first frame - the hand, the tilt, the second person - and leaves the look to the image.

promptExamples.title: Same woman, same outfit, new shot
promptExamples.prompt: Keep the woman from Picture 1 and the black lace slip from Picture 2, in the hotel room from Picture 3. She sits on the arm of the chair, crosses her legs and looks up at camera. Slow handheld drift, warm lamp, quiet room tone.
promptExamples.why: Each photo gets one job and is called by its number, so face, outfit and room carry over instead of blending together.

paramNotes.duration_seconds: Whole seconds, 4 to 30. 2k is limited to 15 seconds, and a clip longer than 15 seconds is billed at twice the per-second rate for the whole clip. Longer clips drift further from a supplied closing frame.
paramNotes.image_url: The opening frame. It sets subject, wardrobe and composition - the model follows it closely. Keep each side between 256 and 5760 px, the aspect ratio between 2:5 and 5:2, and the file under 30 MB.
paramNotes.last_image_url: Optional closing frame. Tightens the ending only; the middle of the clip is still free.
paramNotes.prompt: Describe the change after the opening frame: action, camera, sound. Do not re-describe the frame.
paramNotes.resolution: 480p, 768p or 2k. 480p is a lower-cost draft tier for trying ideas; render the keeper at 768p or 2k. 2k is limited to 15 seconds.

data.readme:
## Introduction

**MiniMax H3 Image to video** starts from an opening frame supplied in `image_url` and generates what happens next: 4 to 30 whole seconds at 480p, 768p or 2k, with sound generated in the same pass. An optional `last_image_url` gives the clip a closing frame to resolve to. There is no aspect-ratio field, because the opening frame sets the shape of the output.

### Choose a MiniMax H3 mode by starting material

| H3 source material | Generation choice |
| --- | --- |
| Scene, action and soundtrack described in words | [MiniMax H3 Text to video](/models/minimax-h3/text-to-video) |
| A chosen first frame whose composition H3 should animate | [MiniMax H3 Image to video](/models/minimax-h3/image-to-video) |
| One to nine pictures assigned to the character, wardrobe or setting | [MiniMax H3 Reference to video](/models/minimax-h3/reference-to-video) |

## Key features & Highlights

### The opening frame decides the subject

The model follows the supplied frame closely, which makes this the most literal way to get the subject, wardrobe and room you designed. In the windowsill-turn example everything identifying, from the face to the outfit to the rain-streaked window, comes from the image; the prompt only asks for an exhale, a neon pulse and a head turn. An opening frame that already shows the scene gets far closer to the brief than the same words typed into text-to-video.

### An optional closing frame

`last_image_url` pins where the shot lands. The doorway example uses both ends: eight seconds that begin inside the room and finish on a supplied doorway composition. The closing frame tightens the ending only. The middle of the clip is still generated freely, and the longer the clip, the further the motion can drift from the closing frame.

### Duration, resolution and input limits

Duration runs from 4 to 30 whole seconds. The resolutions are 480p, 768p and 2k, but 2k is limited to 15 seconds and a longer 2k request is declined with no charge. A clip longer than 15 seconds is billed at twice the per-second rate for the whole clip. The opening frame must measure between 256 and 5,760 px on each side, keep an aspect ratio between 2:5 and 5:2, and stay under 30 MB.

## Use cases

### Animate a still you have already approved

When a frame exists, whether a generated still or an authorised photograph, this endpoint turns it into motion without re-describing it. The prompt carries only the change (action, camera, sound), which keeps every word for what the image cannot say on its own.

### Reveal what the frame does not show

The cup-then-two-in-one-shirt example opens on a still life. A hand lifts the cup out of frame, the camera tilts and racks focus, and a second figure appears deeper in the room: three changes, all temporal, none of them present in the input image. It ran for six seconds, a sensible draft length before a 2k run.

### Continue a scene past 30 seconds

To carry a scene on, use [MiniMax H3 Video extend](/models/minimax-h3/video-extend): it opens the next segment on the final frame of the approved clip and returns the two joined in one file, so each prompt only has to describe what happens next. To steer the next shot frame by frame yourself, take that final frame and submit it here as the next `image_url`.

## Prompt guide & Pro tips

### Do not re-describe the frame

Describe the change after the opening frame and leave appearance to the image. A quick check is that every clause should name something that moves or makes a sound. The windowsill-turn prompt, "she turns her head toward camera without changing expression. Rain runs down the window, distant traffic", is enough because the frame already shows who she is and where.

### Keep the two frames continuous

When you send `last_image_url`, prepare it as a pair with the opening frame: same subject, same wardrobe, same light and a plausible change of framing. Two frames that disagree force the middle of the clip to negotiate between them. Then write the physical action that connects them, as the doorway example does ("rises from the edge of the bed… stops framed in the doorway looking back"), and give that action enough seconds to happen.

### Prepare the frame for the output

Because the frame sets the output shape, crop the still to the delivery aspect ratio before uploading and check it against the size limits. Try ideas at 480p, then re-run the take you want at 480p, 768p or 2k. Expect a new take rather than a frame-for-frame upscale, since the endpoint takes no seed.

examples.note: The opening frame is a still life; everything the prompt asks for happens after it. A hand lifts the cup out of frame, the camera tilts and racks focus, and a second figure appears deeper in the room — three changes, all of them temporal, none of them statable in the input image. That is the split this endpoint rewards: `image_url` owns the composition, and the sentence owns the change.

input.prompt: The cup is lifted out of frame by a hand, then the camera tilts up: she is wearing an oversized men's shirt, and further back in the dim room a man is just getting up. Slow tilt and rack focus. Cinematic, shallow depth of field, heavy film grain, morning grey-gold.

examples.note: One opening frame plus a movement note. Everything identifying - wardrobe, face, room - is decided by the frame, not the words.

input.prompt: She exhales a slow plume of smoke against the rain-streaked glass, the neon outside pulses red across her face, and she turns her head toward camera without changing expression. Rain runs down the window, distant traffic.

examples.note: Both ends pinned, indoors: `image_url` is the opening moment, `last_image_url` is the doorway turn-back she reaches over `duration_seconds` `8`. The `prompt` covers only the walk between — a slow handheld push and footsteps on wood — since the stills already answer what she wears and where she lands. Generate a start and end pose, let the model fill the rest.

input.prompt: She rises from the edge of the bed, lets the silk robe fall closed as she crosses the room, and stops framed in the doorway looking back. Slow handheld push, warm bedside lamp, bare feet on wood.
